newsitem.title: EGYPT: Saudi Arabia blames Israel for summit boycott.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia blames Israel for summit boycott.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal said on Thursday his country was boycotting an Arab-Israeli economic conference in Qatar in November because Israel was threatening the peace process.

Prince Saud also told reporters after meeting Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak that anti-Moslem posters believed to have been pasted in the West Bank town of Hebron by a Jewish woman revealed Israel's true attitude towards Arabs.
Qatar has said it is committed to holding the Middle East/North Africa (MENA) gathering but it has come under pressure from some Arab countries which are angry at Israel's policies about peace.

Saudi Arabian Crown Prince Abdullah in remarks published on Monday said the kingdom would not attend the meeting, the fourth of its kind since the Middle East peace process was launched in 1991, and that Riyadh had advised Qatar to cancel it.
Prince Faisal would not say if his country had advised other Gulf states to boycott the meeting but put the blame squarely on Israel for his country's planned absence.

"We are aware that it is Israeli policy that threatens not only the peace process but the method that has been followed in the context of the peace process including the meetings of the various committees and the multilateral negotiations," Prince Faisal said.
"Saudi Arabia is not striving to take a specific position on any issue, it is Israeli policy that threatens these issues."
Talks between Israel and the Palestinians collapsed in March after the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Arab anger has risen in the divided town of Hebron after the discovery on storefronts on Saturday of anti-Moslem hate posters depicting the Prophet Mohammad as a pig, an animal viewed as unclean by Islam.

Israeli troops, coming under a rain of petrol bombs and rocks, fired rubber-coated metal bullets and wounded 37 Palestinians in Hebron, witnesses said. Soldiers shot dead an Arab teenager in a clash in Gaza.
Israeli leaders have apologised to Palestinian political and religious officials for the posters, which Israeli police say were pasted by a 25-year-old Jewish woman from Jerusalem, now under arrest.
"We believe they (posters) revealed something that has been hidden -- the posters express the Israeli view of the Arab citizen," Prince Faisal said.

"It is a new sign of what must be changed in Israel's thinking and manner if what is wanted is for the peace process to proceed along the correct path. It is a bad sign that expressed a sickness in the Israeli view of Arabs," he added.
